evidence.sourceExcerpt: Fund for Investigative Journalism seed and regular grants - GFMD « Back to all Fundings Fund for Investigative Journalism seed and regular grants Organisation: Fund for Investigative Journalism Status: Open Type: Grant Theme: Investigative journalism Funding Size: $1,000 - $10,000 Deadline: 30/01/2027 Eligibility: Freelance journalists, staff reporters and media outlets in the United States are eligible for grants, and their investigations can be for print, online or broadcast stories, books, documentaries or podcasts. Target Region: North America Application Language: English The Fund for Investigative Journalism provides grants and other support for reporters to produce high-quality, unbiased, nonpartisan investigative stories that have an impact. This application is for seed funding to cover the expenses of preliminary reporting, such as open-records requests and initial reporting trips. Seed Grants for preliminary reporting that can help shape investigative stories. These are also on any topic and for U.S. stories. These grants are up to $2,500 for initial reporting expenses. Journalists who receive seed grants can come back to the Fund to apply for a regular grant, after their preliminary reporting is finished. Eligibility Grants are for preliminary reporting for specific projects. The grants cover early reporting that can lead to full investigative projects. This includes, for example, open-records requests, initial reporting trips to identify and interview sources and the reporter’s time. Grants are $1,000 to $2,500. The entire grant is paid up-front. Journalists who receive seed funding can apply for full grants (up to $10,000) once they conduct the preliminary reporting and secure a commitment from a media outlet to publish or broadcast the story. All information contained in an application is held strictly confidential by the Fund’s board and staff, is shared with no one outside of the organization, and is used solely for the purpose of making a grant decision. Funds are open to freelance journalists and those who are not in full-time staff roles at a media outlet. Seed funding must be used to obtain documents or information that could lead to a full investigative story. The journalist’s time can be one cost covered by the grant, but it should not be the only cost. Other criteria for seed funding mirrors the Fund’s criteria for full grants: stories must be investigative in nature (meaning they uncover wrongdoing that was previously hidden or unknown, and shed light on accountability), and the story must have a very strong U.S. angle. How to apply Apply via the online form for the seed grants. Apply here . For more information, please visit this page. evidence.sourceExcerpt: Equality Fund Global Journalism Fellowship 2026–2027 - GFMD « Back to all Fundings Equality Fund Global Journalism Fellowship 2026–2027 Organisation: Equality Fund Status: Open Type: Fellowship Theme: Gender equality in media Funding Size: CAD 4,000 Deadline: 11/11/2026 Eligibility: five journalists located in ODA-recipient countries Target Region: ODA-eligible countries Application Language: English The Equality Fund has launched its inaugural Global Journalism Fellowship, developed in partnership with Canadian Journalists for Free Expression (CJFE) and African Women in Media (AWiM). The fellowship seeks to surface stories of local solutions to global crises, with a particular focus on gender, by selecting up to five journalists located in ODA-recipient countries. Fellows will spend six months in structured programming followed by three additional months to finalise publication (January–September 2027), receiving a CAD 4,000 stipend, up to CAD 500 in reporting expenses, monthly expert-led online sessions, safety training from the International Women’s Media Foundation (IWMF) and the Freedom of the Press Foundation, and an in-person convening with travel costs covered. The programme is particularly interested in stories that move beyond documenting problems and explore locally driven responses to challenges such as climate change, gender-based violence, economic injustice, conflict, or threats to democracy and human rights. Eligibility Open to full-time or independent freelance journalists working on any journalism platform, including text, digital, video, and audio Minimum of three years of journalism experience Journalists must be located in, and be reporting on, communities in ODA-recipient countries (full country list at oecd.org) Must have three strong journalism samples that showcase a range of relevant work Ability to accommodate meetings within daytime hours in Eastern Standard Time Must be fluent in English, Equality Fund’s working language Must have a strong affinity for the Equality Fund’s mission and values, including equality and diversity of race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, national origin, and disability Women, non-binary, and trans people are encouraged to apply Must have a bank account able to accept international Electronic Wire Transfers Applications from women, men, and LGBTQI+ people are welcomed Use of AI in the proposal and application is not permitted; use of AI during the journalistic process must be disclosed to the programme and approved in advance Requirements Completed online application form submitted before the closing date Three published journalism samples showcasing a range of relevant work In a phased process, shortlisted applicants will be asked to submit a letter of editorial commitment from a news outlet (in some cases of self-publishing, this may be substituted with a fact-checking plan) Fellows must be willing to follow trauma-informed reporting best practices and conduct community roundtables where possible Fellows who are full-time staff journalists will be required to notify their newsroom of the fellowship stipend How to Apply Complete the online application form before 08/11/2026 at midnight Eastern Standard Time. Full application guidelines, including eligibility criteria and programme expectations, are available on the funder’s application page before starting. Apply here . evidence.sourceExcerpt: Call for Proposals - Cross-border Media Literacy (2027) - GFMD « Back to all Fundings Call for Proposals – Cross-border Media Literacy (2027) Organisation: European Commission Status: Open Type: Grant Theme: Media literacy Funding Size: Maximum EUR 500 000 Deadline: 20/01/2027 Eligibility: Consortia composed of at least three entities from a minimum of three different countries participating in the Creative Europe programme Target Region: Europe Application language: English Commission launches Creative Europe Call (EUR 3.5 M) for innovative cross-border media literacy projects, aiming to boost societal resilience against disinformation and information manipulation. In view of the rapidly evolving digital media landscape and the importance of equipping citizens with up-to-date skills and awareness, the European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA) is publishing a call for proposals to support innovative solutions to enhance media literacy skills. The projects shall foster effective cross-border cooperation and enhance societal resilience against disinformation and information manipulation among Europeans. Support will be granted as a priority to initiatives with the potential to reach a broad audience and/or targeted groups currently underserved by media literacy programmes, with a focus on the adult population outside the education system. Eligibility The call is open to consortia composed of at least three entities from a minimum of three different countries participating in the Creative Europe programme. These consortia may include profit and/or non-profit organisations, whether private or public, such as media literacy organisations, public authorities (national, regional, local), universities and educational institutions, media organisations, information integrity organisations, research and technology institutions, technology providers, etc. Support will be granted as a priority to initiatives with the potential to reach a broad audience and/or targeted groups currently underserved by media literacy programmes, with a focus on the adult population outside the education system. Requirements The maximum co-financing rate is 70% of the total eligible costs, so applicants need to co-finance their projects. Projects should address the challenges of a continuously changing digital media landscape. Expected deliverables include creating or scaling up cross-border collaborations that support impactful and innovative approaches to media literacy based on the latest best practices. Expected deliverables include developing and deploying media literacy tools, trainings, campaigns, events and/or other initiatives targeting specific audiences, with a particular focus on adults outside education settings. Expected deliverables include assisting media literacy professionals in adapting their practices to rapidly evolving technological development, media formats and changing media consumption patterns (including the growing role of social media and influencers, AI-generated content, etc.). How to Apply Submit your proposal directly online via the Funding & Tenders Portal Electronic Submission System before 20/01/2027. Paper applications are not accepted. Apply here . evidence.sourceExcerpt: Call for Proposals: Journalism Partnerships - Pluralism (2027) - GFMD « Back to all Fundings Call for Proposals: Journalism Partnerships – Pluralism (2027) Organisation: European Commission Status: Open Type: Grant Theme: Media support Funding Size: Maximum EUR 2.5 million Deadline: 04/02/2027 Eligibility: European intermediary organisations that set up and distribute funds Target Region: Europe Application language: English This call supports intermediary organisations that set up and distribute funds to news media in sectors of particular relevance to democracy, such as local and regional media, community media, investigative journalism, and public interest news. Projects are expected to start towards the end of 2027 and last 24 months. Eligibility The call relies on intermediary organisations active in the media domain. Financial support will be awarded to these organisations so that they can set up financing schemes for news media sectors in need. The call is open to entities such as media associations, NGOs, non-profit organisations, civil society organisations, public authorities, international organisations, universities, research centres, journalistic funds and training organisations focusing on media professionals, profitmaking entities, foundations, etc. Proposals may be submitted either by single applicants or by a consortium. The funding schemes must focus on the European Union, and specifically on areas with low provision of the specific news described above, or in media markets where media pluralism is strained. Funding schemes should target news media sectors of special relevance to democracy and civic participation, characterised by their role in enhancing democracy, shaping the public debate and bringing benefits to their audiences and communities, instead of focusing just on profit. These sectors include in particular local and regional media; independent and investigative journalism; and organisations delivering public interest news/public service journalism (such as community, legal and civic journalism and media, news increasing transparency about the media). Requirements Setting up a funding scheme for media organisations is compulsory. The maximum co-financing rate is 90% of the total eligible costs, so applicants need to co-finance their projects (but their grantees should not be required to co-finance). The funds can focus on activities that contribute to transforming the work of targeted parties, for instance innovations in editorial production, news coverage and revenue models; improvement of distribution and dissemination of news; audience development and engagement and community-building strategies; development of technical tools; and training on these topics. Applicants can also propose accompanying activities to the fund (development of standards, indicators, repositories of knowledge, legal advice, trainings, etc). How to Apply Submit your proposal directly online via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal Electronic Submission System before 04/02/2027. Paper applications are not accepted. Proposals will be evaluated in spring, and results communicated in summer 2027. Apply here . For more information, please visit this page . evidence.sourceExcerpt: Call for Proposals: Journalism Partnerships - Collaborations (2027) - GFMD « Back to all Fundings Call for Proposals: Journalism Partnerships – Collaborations (2027) Organisation: European Commission Status: Open Type: Grant Theme: Media Innovation Funding Size: maximum EUR 2 million Deadline: 04/02/2027 Eligibility: European news media Target Region: Europe Application language: English This 7th annual call supports cross-border, collaborative proposals between news media organisations focusing on innovative business models and/or journalistic projects across Europe. It aims to help European news media become more sustainable and resilient by supporting cross-border media collaborations. Projects are expected to last 24 months. Eligibility Consortia may include non-profit, public and private media outlets (including written/online press, radio/podcasts, TV) as well as other organisations focusing on news media (including media associations, NGOs, journalistic funds and training organisations focusing on media professionals). Natural persons are not eligible (with the exception of self-employed persons, i.e. sole traders, where the company does not have legal personality separate from that of the natural person). Consortia must gather at least 3 partners from at least 3 different countries participating in the Creative Europe Programme. Since the opening intends to achieve sector-wide impacts, proposals are invited to involve as many news media as possible in their activities. Consortia may choose to focus on a news media (sub)sector (for example tv, radio, printed press) and/or journalistic genre (for example, data journalism, specialised journalism). Requirements The maximum co-financing rate is 80% of the total eligible costs, so applicants need to co-finance their projects. Applicants are called to set up cross-border media collaborations, for example to develop better revenue and monetisation models, new approaches to audience development, community-building and marketing, common professional/technical standards, new types of newsrooms, syndication networks or other models to exchange content/data between news media across the EU, or to provide assistance to small media organisations. Proposals should include activities that best contribute to the consortium’s goals, such as events, online trainings and workshops, exchange programmes, mentoring schemes, mapping of best practices, development of technical standards, guidelines and editorial standards, practical guidebooks, development and testing of platforms and technical solutions, and promotional activities. Financial support to third parties is allowed for grants and prizes under the conditions set in the call. How to Apply Submit your proposal directly online via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal Electronic Submission System before 04/02/2027. Paper applications are not accepted. Proposals will be evaluated in spring, and results communicated in summer 2027. Apply here . For more information, please visit this page .
